findings.title: Fallback locales are only loaded in the web request path, not in jobs or mailers
findings.body: With the accelerator patch, translations load on demand. `I18n.translate` only loads `config.locale`, and the fallback locales (site default and `:en`) are loaded only by `I18n.fallbacks.ensure_loaded!`. That call happens solely in `ApplicationController#set_locale`. Sidekiq jobs, mailers, rake tasks and other non-controller code never call it. In those contexts the Fallbacks backend looks up keys in locales that were never loaded and gets nil, so fallbacks silently do not work and users see 'translation missing' text. The fallback locales should be loaded inside `I18n.translate`/`load_locale`, not in a controller filter.

findings.title: Translation cache key ignores the fallback chain, so stale or missing results stay cached
findings.body: Results now depend on the fallback chain: `SiteSetting.default_locale`, plus which fallback locales happen to be loaded. The LRU cache key is still only key + `config.locale` + backend id. Two problems follow. (1) If the site's default locale changes, cached fallback strings from the old default locale keep being served until the process restarts or the entry is evicted. (2) If a key is translated before the fallback locales are loaded (e.g. outside a controller), the 'translation missing' result is frozen into the cache. It is then returned even after the fallback locales are loaded. The cache key should include the fallback chain, or the cache should be cleared when the default locale changes.

findings.title: SiteSetting lookup on every fallback resolution
findings.body: `FallbackLocaleList#[]` builds a new array and reads `SiteSetting.default_locale` on every call. The Fallbacks backend calls it on every uncached translate, which includes every translate call that has interpolation or count arguments, since those bypass the LRU cache. This allocates a new array on every one of those calls and adds avoidable overhead to a very hot path.

findings.title: No tests for new fallback behavior
findings.body: The PR changes translation resolution for every locale but adds no specs. Untested cases include: fallback to the site locale then to English, loading of the fallback locales, and behavior in non-request contexts. Regressions such as the missing-load issue in jobs would go unnoticed.
